Priya: Heads up - CI perf unit flagged a regression in kernel_selector perf test on PR #18820.
Priya: microbench reported 3.1x allocation increase and p99 latency jump.
CI-bot: [ci] run https://ci.internal/runs/77321 finished: perf-fail
CI-bot: Summary: kernel_selector_test::AffinityAllocation: baseline=18ms p99 / allocs=4.5k -> current=47ms / allocs=14k (threshold +120%)
Alex: that's huge, probably memory churn from the new affinity allocator heuristics.
Sam: did a quick bisect on local reproducer: commit abcdef1 (merge PR #18820) flips allocator path. Repro script: `tools/perf/repro_affinity.sh --seed=42`
Sam: I attached flamegraph snapshot: alloc hot path is `KernelSelector::pick()` -> `AffinitySampler::reserve()`
Maria: PR 18820 added a small cache in kernel selector but changed lifetime semantics; maybe double-copying KV entries on warmup.
Devon: can someone try reverting the small cache change as a hotfix to see CI delta? If it fixes, we'll block the rollout.
Priya: I'll queue a revert PR now. @Alex @Sam can you validate on perf runner? If revert fixes, mark PR 18820 as rollback and hold the release.
Alex: running on perf runner now, linking run 77328 — will update in ~15m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sam: quick note: repro is noisy; add `--iterations=50` to repro script to stabilize.
CI-bot: perf-run 77328 results: p99=20ms allocs=5.1k (within threshold). Looks like revert candidate reduces spike.
Priya: Great. Creating revert PR 18857 and tagging eng-runtime/rollback. Also filing a follow-up to properly fix lifetime vs copy semantics.
Devon: I'll prepare a small test-case to catch this regression in presubmit (alloc regression guard).
Priya: Thanks team — blocking mergewindow until we confirm fix on CI. :lock:
